# mtncloud_archive_file (Resource)

A file in an archive (Tools > Archives), up to 512 MiB, kept in the archive's MOS bucket. Changing its content uploads it again; the file keeps its ID. Its folders are made on the way. Destroy deletes the file, not the folders it is in.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "mtncloud_archive_file" "readme" {
  archive = mtncloud_archive_bucket.exports.name
  path    = "docs/README.txt"
  content = "Nightly exports land here.\n"
}

# By the archive's ID, from a local file: editing the file uploads it again.
resource "mtncloud_archive_file" "report" {
  archive_id = mtncloud_archive_bucket.exports.id
  path       = "reports/2026/october.pdf"
  source     = "${path.module}/october.pdf"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `path` (String) The file's path in the archive, for example `reports/2026/october.pdf`, with no `/` at either end. Changing it replaces the file.

### Optional

- `archive` (String) The archive, by name (`mtncloud_archive_bucket.x.name`). Set this or `archive_id`. Another archive replaces the file. When the archive may be renamed, use `archive_id`: a new name can't be matched to the old one at plan time, so the file would be uploaded again.
- `archive_id` (String) The archive, by ID (`mtncloud_archive_bucket.x.id`). Set this or `archive`. Another archive replaces the file.
- `content` (String) The content, as text. Set one of `content`, `content_base64` and `source`.
- `content_base64` (String) The content, base64-encoded, for binary data.
- `source` (String) A local file to upload. Its content is compared at every plan, so editing the file uploads it again.

### Read-Only

- `content_sha256` (String) The SHA-256 of the content Terraform uploaded, in hex. Empty after the file was changed outside Terraform (its size changed), so the next apply uploads it again.
- `content_type` (String) The content type the archive serves the file with.
- `id` (String) The file's ID.
- `last_updated` (String) When the file was last written (RFC 3339).
- `size_bytes` (Number) The file's size in bytes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By the file's ID, or by <archive>/<path>.
terraform import mtncloud_archive_file.readme 1626
terraform import mtncloud_archive_file.readme acme-exports/docs/README.txt
```
